[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/HelloWorldFlutterApp/sha/b48656572b3ebfe121715fcdace4d3b0fbbdded6/contents/.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml] # Claudinite per-repo task scheduler — the repo's ONLY cron
# (per-project-scheduling DESIGN §3). A thin shim: all logic lives in the
# vendored engine, so this file changes rarely (schema and behavior changes ride
# the vendor refresh, not edits here). It runs hourly on a repo-hashed minute
# constrained to :10–:50 — spreading the fleet, dodging GitHub's :00 stampede,
# and staying clear of the hour boundary the slot math anchors on.
#
# The minute below is a placeholder; bootstrap/vendoring rewrites it to this
# repo's stable hashed minute in :10–:50, computed by
# `node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs <owner/repo>`
# (scheduler-workflow-shape enforces the range; baselining re-derives the value to
# catch drift). `workflow_dispatch` allows a manual run; the concurrency group
# serializes runs so a slow run and its successor never overlap.
#
# A manual run may carry `overrides` — ONE free-form `KEY=value` string, because
# GitHub cannot declare arbitrary named inputs. It reaches the engine as
# `CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES`, and the engine understands exactly one key:
# `FORCE_TASKS=<comma-separated task ids>`.
# It runs those tasks even though their slot has already passed, and
# WITHOUT consulting their preconditions — forcing is the operator's decision, so
# nothing asks the task whether it agrees. The engine learns "run these ids",
# never what any of them do, and no task declaration mentions forcing at all.
name: Claudinite scheduler

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '30 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      overrides:
        description: 'Manual-run overrides: comma-separated KEY=value. FORCE_TASKS=<task ids> runs those tasks unconditionally, even when their slot has passed, e.g. FORCE_TASKS=baselining.'
        required: false
        default: ''

concurrency:
  group: claudinite-scheduler
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write        # read the repo + vendored engine; baselining's deliver() pushes the maintenance branch (agent-preprocessing §7/E4)
  issues: write          # file / label / close dispatch issues
  pull-requests: write   # baselining's deliver() opens the per-cycle maintenance PR and arms auto-merge
  actions: write         # read the run ledger (last successful run) for due-slot math, AND
                         # dispatch a workflow a task drives (store-release fires the release
                         # orchestrator's daily leg) — creating a workflow_dispatch event needs
                         # write, not read, and `read` silently 403s the POST

jobs:
  schedule:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Evaluate schedule and dispatch due tasks
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # Empty on every scheduled run — `inputs` is only populated by
          # workflow_dispatch. The engine reads only FORCE_TASKS out of it.
          CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES: ${{ inputs.overrides }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/run.mjs

  # A scheduled run reaches no one when it goes red, so escalate a whole-run
  # failure to a human-visible `workflow-failure` issue (DESIGN §3.6,
  # gha/scheduled-failure-escalation). Converges to ONE open issue by a fixed
  # title (create-or-comment), and ensures the label first since a first-run
  # failure may precede the scheduler's own label-ensure.
  report-failure:
    needs: schedule
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const { owner, repo } = context.repo;
            const title = 'Claudinite scheduler run failed';
            await github.rest.issues.createLabel({ owner, repo, name: 'workflow-failure', color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite scheduler: a scheduler run or task failed' }).catch(() => {});
            const run = `${context.serverUrl}/${owner}/${repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`;
            const body = `The Claudinite scheduler run failed: ${run}`;
            const found = await github.rest.search.issuesAndPullRequests({ q: `repo:${owner}/${repo} is:issue is:open in:title "${title}"` });
            if (found.data.total_count > 0) await github.rest.issues.createComment({ owner, repo, issue_number: found.data.items[0].number, body });
            else await github.rest.issues.create({ owner, repo, title, labels: ['workflow-failure'], body });

[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/hitbut/sha/03f34fcccff1e3ce611aeb5a2732aea164d71c63/contents/.github/workflows/product.yml] # hitbut's own build: the requirements suite, and the deploy that ships `main`.
name: product

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: product-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  checks:
    name: requirements (logic, behavior, server)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run typecheck
      # Watch the count, not the colour: a run that finds no tests exits green.
      - run: npm test
      - run: npm run test:server
      # Phase 0's exit condition that needs no account: the committed wrangler.toml
      # builds and its bindings resolve.
      - run: npx wrangler deploy --dry-run --outdir "$RUNNER_TEMP/dry-run"

  screen:
    name: requirements (screen)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Pinned to the Playwright the goldens were rendered with. A different build
    # rasterises text differently, and the comparison would measure the renderer.
    container: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.56.1-noble
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run test:screen
      - name: The pictures, when they disagree
        if: failure()
        # v6, not v5 like the actions above: upload-artifact's v5 still runs on
        # Node 20, so matching the others here would leave the deprecation in
        # place on the one step that only runs when something is already wrong.
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v6
        with:
          name: screen-failures
          path: dev/requirements/failures/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  deploy:
    name: ship main
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    needs: [checks, screen]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
      CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - name: Is there an account to deploy to yet?
        id: account
        run: |
          if [ -z "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] || [ -z "$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" ]; then
            echo "Cloudflare provisioning (issue #27) has not landed — nothing to deploy yet."
            echo "ready=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "ready=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      - if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        run: npm ci
      # Turns "the deploy failed somewhere in wrangler" into a named missing resource.
      # Everything it can report missing is one run of the *provision* workflow away.
      - name: Does production exist?
        if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        run: npm run preflight
      - name: Bring the corpus schema up to date
        if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        run: npm run corpus:migrate:remote
      # Each deploy step reads its origin back and exports it, so the site is built against
      # the API that was just deployed and the smoke test knows where to look. A repository
      # variable is an override for a custom domain, not something the first deploy needs.
      - name: Deploy the Worker
        if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        env:
          API_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.API_ORIGIN }}
        run: npm run deploy:api
      - name: Build the site against the deployed API
        if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        run: VITE_API_ORIGIN="$API_ORIGIN" npm run build:site
      - name: Deploy the site
        if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        env:
          SITE_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.SITE_ORIGIN }}
        run: npm run deploy:site
      # Everything the suite proves is proven against a local workerd. This is the only
      # step that reads what actually shipped.
      - name: Does what shipped answer?
        if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        run: npm run smoke

[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/TLDR/sha/578ab8ab92f8f0659b0b6bf56ae113802745eb5d/contents/README.md] # TLDR

<!-- claudinite:packs -->
![basics](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-mTVfQ3/packs/basics/badge.svg "basics") ![barriers](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-mTVfQ3/packs/barriers/badge.svg "barriers") ![git-github](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-mTVfQ3/packs/git-github/badge.svg "git-github") ![chrome-extension](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-mTVfQ3/packs/chrome-extension/badge.svg "chrome-extension") ![chrome-extension-release](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-mTVfQ3/packs/chrome-extension-release/badge.svg "chrome-extension-release") ![executable-requirements](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-mTVfQ3/packs/executable-requirements/badge.svg "executable-requirements") ![github-actions](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-mTVfQ3/packs/github-actions/badge.svg "github-actions") ![node](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-mTVfQ3/packs/node/badge.svg "node") ![spec-driven-product](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-mTVfQ3/packs/spec-driven-product/badge.svg "spec-driven-product") ![tidy-repo](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-mTVfQ3/packs/tidy-repo/badge.svg "tidy-repo") ![grow_with_claudinite](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-mTVfQ3/packs/grow_with_claudinite/badge.svg "grow_with_claudinite")<!-- /claudinite:packs -->

Get community-generated tl;dr notes for any link on the web — a Chrome extension where signed-in users
read and post short notes ("comments") attached to any page, keyed by its normalized URL.

This is a monorepo with an AWS backend and an MV3 Chrome extension, wired together by a single shared
URL-normalization rule.

## Install

**[Install from the Chrome Web Store →](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/tldr-%E2%80%94-community-notes/cgfkbaigkiccdpnmmbfmookalaombhil)**

Or load the latest development build:

1. Download [the latest release zip](https://github.com/missingbulb/TLDR/releases/latest/download/tldr.zip)
   and extract it — it unpacks to a folder with `manifest.json` at its top. (This download is
   dev-pointed, like a plain checkout; only the Chrome Web Store build is prod-pointed — see
   [`dev/docs/extension.md`](dev/docs/extension.md).)
2. Open `chrome://extensions`, enable **Developer mode** (top right), click
   **Load unpacked**, and select that folder.

## Releasing

The version users see is [`extension/manifest.json`](extension/manifest.json)'s `version`. Merging a
version bump to `main` cuts GitHub Release `vX.Y.Z` with `tldr.zip` attached, and the daily
auto-release ships shipped-file changes to the Chrome Web Store on its own (patch-bumping as
needed).

## Layout
| Path | What |
|------|------|
| [`shared/`](shared/normalizeUrl.mjs) | The single source of truth for URL → `pageId` normalization (vendored into both sides, drift-guarded); `shared/test/` holds its corpus test. |
| [`server/`](server/README.md) | Everything AWS: HTTP API + Google JWT authorizer, one Lambda, DynamoDB. One CloudFormation stack. |
| [`extension/`](dev/docs/extension.md) | The MV3 Chrome extension (side panel, no bundler). |
| [`dev/requirements/`](dev/requirements/README.md) | The executable-requirements suite (client UI + server), spanning both apps. |
| [`dev/docs/`](dev/docs/architecture.md) | The as-built [architecture](dev/docs/architecture.md) + the portable [UI-testing guideline](dev/docs/ui-testing-guideline.md). |
| [`dev/build/tools/`](dev/build/tools/sync-shared.mjs) | Build tooling: the shared-code sync + its drift guard (`dev/build/tools/test/`). |
| `.github/workflows/` | CI (`server`, `extension`, `requirements`), gated deploy (`deploy`), and the single extension-release stub (`release`) whose jobs call the Claudinite canon reusable workflows (create-package, publish, daily; privacy-page deploy and failure reporting live in the canon). |

## Architecture in one breath
Public reads; authenticated writes. The client fetches only while the side panel is open,
for the active tab, and only on commentable pages. A comment is one DynamoDB item keyed by
`(pageId, ULID)`, so "all comments for a page" is a single-partition query. See
[`dev/docs/architecture.md`](dev/docs/architecture.md).

## Quickstart (owner setup)
The code is complete; bringing it live needs five owner-specific inputs (none can be defaulted):

1. **Google OAuth "Web application" client** → its client id. (`server/README.md` §1)
2. **AWS deploy role via GitHub OIDC** → set repo variable `AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN` (+ `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`). (`server/README.md` §2)
3. `cd server && sam build && sam deploy …`. (`server/README.md` §3)
4. Set the client config as repo **variables** (`API_BASE_URL`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `EXTENSION_PUBLIC_KEY`) — the
   release build injects them into the zip; committed source stays placeholder. (`dev/docs/extension.md`)
5. Release: bump the version on `main` (that runs the **create-package** job) + run the **Release**
   workflow with **mode: publish**; once live, the daily auto-release ships changes on its own. The
   zip is built in CI.

Open product/config questions are tracked in [`dev/docs/architecture.md`](dev/docs/architecture.md) §11.

## Develop & test
```bash
npm test                       # repo-level checks: URL-normalizer corpus + shared drift guard
npm --prefix server ci && npm --prefix server test
npm --prefix extension test    # extension unit + manifest/packaging guards (no deps)
npm --prefix dev ci && npm --prefix dev test           # the executable-requirements suite (UI + server)
```
No bundler, no linter — native `node --test` and `node --check`, matching the project's conventions.
The UI + server requirements are specified as executable requirements under
[`dev/requirements/`](dev/requirements/README.md); regenerate its rendered images with
`npm --prefix dev run refresh:ui` after an intentional panel change.

[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/Shepherd/sha/340cae206084f615fc9436590c08f2dee0974743/contents/.github/workflows/claudinite-dashboard-pages.yml] # Publish the Claudinite task dashboard to GitHub Pages.
#
# SEEDED ONCE, AT ADOPTION, and this repo's from that moment. `.github/workflows/` is
# the one directory the nightly update cannot push to — the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` is
# refused there — so this file arrives with the adopting session and never converges.
# That is why it is a thin shim: everything that can be updated lives in the mount, and
# only what must be frozen is frozen here.
#
# The site holds NO repository data. It is a shell that calls the GitHub API from the
# viewer's own browser with the viewer's own credential, so publishing it discloses
# nothing a viewer could not already read — someone who cannot see a repo sees nothing
# of it here. Do not bake API responses into the build; that property is the reason a
# public Pages site is a safe host for it.
#
# Configure it in `.claudinite-checks.json`, on the `claudinite-dashboard` entry's
# `config` — not here. Every key is optional.

name: Claudinite dashboard

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      # The mount is the page's source, so a converge that moves it republishes.
      - '.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-dashboard/**'
      - '.claudinite/shared/engine/**'
      - '.claudinite-checks.json'
      - '.github/workflows/claudinite-dashboard-pages.yml'
  # The push trigger above cannot see the one push that moves the mount most often.
  # Claudinite's own update PRs are auto-merged by the Actions token, and a push made
  # with `GITHUB_TOKEN` deliberately fires no workflow — so every converge lands
  # silently and the site keeps serving whatever the last human merge built.
  #
  # The catch-up hangs off the scheduler rather than a `cron:` of its own, because the
  # vendored scheduler is this repo's one permitted schedule. Following it is not
  # competing with it: the cadence stays the scheduler's, and this only asks, each time
  # it finishes, whether the page's sources have moved since the last deploy.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Claudinite scheduler']
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Never two deployments at once, and a superseded build is not worth finishing.
concurrency:
  group: claudinite-dashboard-pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      # The scheduler finishes every hour, and on almost all of those the page's
      # sources are exactly what was deployed last time. A cache entry keyed on those
      # sources is the cheapest available answer to "has anything moved": a hit means
      # this same tree is already live, and the run stops here. The entry is written
      # only once the deploy has succeeded, so a failed one is retried rather than
      # recorded as done. A `push` or a hand dispatch skips the question — those are
      # asked for, and a forced republish must not be answered with a cache hit.
      - name: What the page would be built from
        id: sources
        run: echo "key=dashboard-deployed-${{ hashFiles('.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-dashboard/**', '.claudinite/shared/engine/**', '.claudinite-checks.json', '**/*.GENERATED.json') }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Is that already deployed?
        id: deployed
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_run'
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: .deployed
          key: ${{ steps.sources.outputs.key }}
          lookup-only: true

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        if: steps.deployed.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        with:
          node-version: 24

      - name: Assemble the site
        if: steps.deployed.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-dashboard/build-site.mjs

      # The build exits clean with no `_site` when the mount does not yet carry the
      # dashboard — adopted, not yet converged. Uploading nothing would fail the run,
      # and deploying an empty artifact would replace a working site with a 404.
      - name: Is there a site to publish?
        id: built
        if: steps.deployed.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: |
          if [ -f _site/index.html ]; then
            echo "ready=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "ready=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "No _site/index.html — skipping the deploy until the mount carries the dashboard."
          fi

      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
        if: steps.built.outputs.ready == 'true'

      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        if: steps.built.outputs.ready == 'true'
        with:
          path: _site

    outputs:
      ready: ${{ steps.built.outputs.ready }}
      key: ${{ steps.sources.outputs.key }}

  deploy:
    needs: build
    if: needs.build.outputs.ready == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

      # Now, and only now, is this tree deployed — which is what the next scheduler
      # wake-up reads to decide it has nothing to do.
      - run: mkdir -p .deployed && echo "${{ github.sha }}" > .deployed/sha
      - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: .deployed
          key: ${{ needs.build.outputs.key }}

[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/Shepherd/sha/340cae206084f615fc9436590c08f2dee0974743/contents/.github/workflows/checks.yml] # The repo's test/CI flow. Today it holds one step: the Claudinite WORLD-SCOPE
# sweep (bootstrap.md Part 8) — a whole-repo invariant assertion, the same shape as
# a test suite, so a red sweep fails this flow exactly like a failing test would.
# The WORK scope is not here: it judges a session's own change and runs at that
# session's Stop hook.
#
# When this repo grows tests of its own, they go in as further steps of this job —
# not as a second workflow.
name: Checks

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # The sweep's default scope compares against origin/main, so the
          # history it measures from has to be here.
          fetch-depth: 0

[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/gRatio/sha/163a2b8c91e524dc5dd793b69dc93ec320917246/contents/README.md] # gRatio — area-based myelin g-ratio from EM cross-sections

<!-- claudinite:packs -->
![basics](.claudinite/shared/packs/basics/badge.svg "basics") ![barriers](.claudinite/shared/packs/barriers/badge.svg "barriers") ![git-github](.claudinite/shared/packs/git-github/badge.svg "git-github") ![research-project](.claudinite/shared/packs/research-project/badge.svg "research-project") ![tidy-repo](.claudinite/shared/packs/tidy-repo/badge.svg "tidy-repo") ![grow_with_claudinite](.claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/badge.svg "grow_with_claudinite")<!-- /claudinite:packs -->

Computes the myelin **g-ratio** from electron-microscopy cross-sections of
axons, using an **area-based** definition that is robust to malformed /
non-hermetic myelin.

## Why area-based

The classical g-ratio is a ratio of diameters (inner axon / outer fiber)
measured along one chosen direction. That makes it sensitive to *which*
cross-section and *which* diameter you measure, and it is skewed when the myelin
does not hermetically enclose the axon (the missing myelin is invisible to a
diameter measured elsewhere). Areas are direction-independent, and measuring the
**actual myelin material present** lets malformed myelin correctly lower the
apparent sheath:

```
g = sqrt( A_axon / (A_axon + A_myelin) )        # textbook convention, value < 1
```

- `A_axon` — area of the axon interior (lumen).
- `A_myelin` — area of the actual myelin material around that axon.

On a perfectly circular, hermetically myelinated axon, `sqrt` of the area ratio
equals the radius ratio, so this reproduces the standard diameter-based g-ratio
exactly (**parity**); it only diverges when the myelin is malformed — which is
the point. Background and the full derivation, plus how this relates to the
MyelTracer reference tool, are in
[`docs/reference/myeltracer_notes.md`](docs/reference/myeltracer_notes.md).

## Usage

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt

# write overlays + per-axon CSVs to outputs/
python analyze.py data/samples/*.png -o outputs/

# tunables can be overridden, e.g.
python analyze.py data/samples/sample_02.png -o outputs/ --myelin-percentile 25
```

Each input produces a side-by-side `<name>_gratio.png` (left: the original;
right: the overlay) and `<name>_gratio.csv` (per-axon `g_ratio`,
`axon_area_px`, `myelin_area_px`, centroid, equivalent radius, solidity). In the
overlay, **each axon+myelin pair gets its own colour**, the axon body is drawn
with a white (inner) border, the myelin band with a coloured (outer) border —
both **smooth, roughly-closed shapes**, not pixel-following outlines —
**bubbles** (holes / missing myelin in the sheath) are filled red, and the
g-ratio is printed at the axon centroid. Use `--overlay-only` to skip the
side-by-side.

Programmatic use:

```python
import cv2
from gratio import segment, render, render_comparison
gray = cv2.cvtColor(cv2.imread("img.png"), cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
seg = segment(gray)
for a in seg["axons"]:
    print(a["id"], a["g"])
comparison = render_comparison(gray, seg)   # original | overlay
```

## Structural model

Each fiber is a set of contiguous bodies with **smooth, roughly-closed borders**
(not strict ovals, and not intricate pixel-following outlines):

- **axon** — a smoothed bright body (the axoplasm); its border is the inner
  border of the myelin.
- **myelin** — a smoothed band around the axon, of bounded thickness; a band
  shared by touching fibers is split by nearest axon, so neighbours are not
  confused.
- **bubble** — a *significant* bright hole in the band (a vacuole, or a stretch
  of missing / non-hermetic myelin). Bubbles are **not** myelin: they are
  excluded from `A_myelin` and highlighted, because they are exactly the
  malformation we want to surface.

## How it works

1. grayscale + bilateral filter (edge-preserving denoise)
2. myelin mask = darkest pixels (percentile threshold); remove speckle
3. fiber region = myelin closed enough to **seal broken rings**, then
   hole-filled — this isolates each axon's bright body from the background even
   when the surrounding ring is incomplete (the malformed case)
4. axon bodies = bright bodies inside fibers passing area / solidity / brightness
5. myelin = dark band touching an axon, within a thickness cap; a band shared by
   touching fibers is split by nearest axon
6. smooth the axon body and the (axon ∪ myelin) region into roughly-closed shapes
7. bubbles = significant bright holes in the smoothed annulus; excluded from myelin
8. g per axon from the area formula above

The g-ratio is **dimensionless**, so no spatial calibration is needed; the
sample images' scale bars are not used.

## Status

Working prototype, validated against **hand-drawn ground-truth masks** of the
three sample micrographs. The segmentation runs on the raw grayscale images and
is scored by mask overlap (IoU) — current means: **axon 0.94 / myelin 0.87 /
fibre 0.96, detection recall & precision 1.00** (baseline before tuning was
0.74 / 0.51 / 0.80, recall 0.80). Run `python evaluate_segmentation.py`.

New to the project? Read these first:

- [`docs/reference/requirements.md`](docs/reference/requirements.md) — the
  project owner's requirements, gathered from the working sessions.
- [`docs/reference/continuation.md`](docs/reference/continuation.md) — how to
  resume: current state, how to run, the tuned parameters and why, open items.
- [`docs/reference/user_masks.md`](docs/reference/user_masks.md) — full method
  narrative, per-sample results, and the ground-truth registration.

**Open issues / next steps.**
- *Malformed-axon boundary.* Where the ring is badly broken (left side of the
  central `sample_01` axon), the bright axoplasm merges with extracellular space
  through the gap, so the sealed-ring boundary over-extends. The axon is
  detected and bordered, but its boundary there is approximate — this is the
  inherently hard region and the next target (axon-boundary refinement,
  interactive seeding, or an ML segmenter such as AxonDeepSeg).
- *Gap-fill scale.* `myelin_close` decides which gaps are "normal inter-lamellar
  spacing" (filled, counted as myelin) vs "malformation" (left open, excluded).
  This threshold directly affects g for loosely-myelinated axons and is a
  modelling choice worth calibrating against expert tracing.

## Validation & tests

A baseline of **regular** axons with **known** g-ratios is mirrored in
`data/reference/axondeepseg_sem/` — real SEM cross-sections of rat spinal cord
with manual axon/myelin masks (AxonDeepSeg, MIT). `gratio/reference.py` computes
the trusted per-axon g-ratio directly from those masks
(`g = sqrt(axon_area / (axon_area + myelin_area))`); across 1642 axons the mean
is **0.655** (per-sample 0.61–0.69), i.e. textbook-normal.

```bash
pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
python -m pytest -q          # synthetic exact-answer + real ground-truth regression tests
```

Tests cover (a) synthetic perfect annuli where `g = r_in/r_out` exactly, and
(b) regression on the real ground-truth distribution. The image **pipeline** is
not yet benchmarked against this ground truth — that is the next step, and note
the SEM data has **inverted contrast** (bright myelin) vs. the TEM samples.

## Layout

```
gratio/pipeline.py            core: segment(), render(), analyze_image(), DEFAULTS
gratio/reference.py           ground-truth g-ratio from segmentation masks
analyze.py                    CLI
data/samples/                 sample TEM micrographs (the user's images)
data/reference/axondeepseg_sem/  regular-axon SEM images + masks + ground-truth g
outputs/                      example overlays + CSVs
tests/                        synthetic + ground-truth regression tests
docs/reference/               distilled notes + figures from the MyelTracer paper
```

Weekly `canon-curation/growth-discover-packs` fleet sweep (#1279), Context-scoped to 16 members.

## The gap

`missingbulb/hitbut` is the fleet's first Cloudflare Workers backend — a single Worker bound to
D1, R2, Vectorize and Queues, deployed and tested with Wrangler (`src/backend/`,
`dev/requirements/server/`, `dev/tools/preflight.ts`/`smoke.ts`). No canon pack homes Cloudflare
Workers, and the repo demonstrates real, portable gotchas with no false-positive-free static
signature — deploy-vs-migration ordering, a hand-declared `env.ts` avoiding a Workers-types/DOM
collision once a frontend shares the repo, testing against real `workerd` from the committed
`wrangler.toml`, seeding D1 from the shipped migration files, why local Wrangler emulation can't
prove Cloudflare's own D1/R2/Queues, and parsing a Wrangler preflight's own error markers to tell
*missing* from *unknown*.

Single-member evidence, but per the worthiness bar this is the weaker-but-qualifying case: the
knowledge is plainly general (any future Cloudflare Workers project would want every rule here),
not this product's non-transferable particulars. Stripped of hitbut's product vocabulary
(persona/utterance/finding/corpus never appear).

## What's in this PR

- `packs/cloudflare-workers/` — `RULES.md` (7 rules), `pack.mjs` (fingerprint: a
  `wrangler.toml`/`.jsonc`/`.json` at the repo root or one directory down), `README.md`
  (rule index + provenance), `badge.svg`.
- `packs/README.md` — index row.
- `packs/directory.GENERATED.md` — regenerated (`node --test engine-tests/pack-directory.test.mjs`).

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2663 pass, 0 fail (the one pre-existing shallow-clone
  failure on `main` also cleared on this checkout).
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking, exit 0; no findings on the new pack.

## Follow-ups (tracker only, not this PR)

- `missingbulb/LaughCounter` and `missingbulb/WIP` already carry the fingerprint for the existing
  `macos` and `flutter` packs respectively but haven't declared them; `missingbulb/TLDR` likewise
  for `aws-sam`. Left for the fingerprint sweep (`fleet-add-missing-packs`), per the task's own
  rule that a homed technology gets a "should declare" tracker note, never a new pack or an issue
  from this run.
- `missingbulb/EdFringeAllocator` calls the Anthropic API directly for its LLM scheduler, but the
  evidence is one thin script with no recurring gotcha beyond ordinary API-calling practice —
  considered and rejected as too shallow for a pack.

Logged to #642 (`Claudinite tracker: Discover Canon Packs`).

[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/TLDR/sha/578ab8ab92f8f0659b0b6bf56ae113802745eb5d/contents/server/template.yaml] AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31
Description: >
  TLDR backend (app stack) — HTTP API v2 + Google JWT authorizer, one Lambda, DynamoDB single table.

Parameters:
  GoogleClientId:
    Type: String
    # Intentionally no default: an empty JWT-authorizer audience would accept ID tokens minted for
    # ANY Google app. This MUST be the Google Cloud OAuth "Web application" client id.
    Description: Google OAuth "Web application" client id — the JWT authorizer audience (also the extension's auth client_id).
    AllowedPattern: '.+'
    ConstraintDescription: GoogleClientId must be provided.
  AllowedExtensionOrigin:
    Type: String
    Default: '*'
    Description: >
      CORS allowed origin. Keep '*': API Gateway HTTP API v2 REJECTS the chrome-extension:// scheme in CORS
      AllowOrigins ("Invalid format for origin"), so the extension origin can't be set here. Not a security
      gap — writes are gated by the JWT authorizer and reads are public; the '*' is also what lets the
      extension reach the API under standard CORS (so it needs no host_permissions). The security boundary is
      the JWT authorizer, never browser CORS. (See dev/docs/architecture.md §6.3 / §12-A9 / §12-A10.)
  RateLimitPerMinute:
    Type: Number
    Default: 10
    Description: Max comments one author may post per minute (enforced by a TTL'd DynamoDB counter). 0 disables.
  MaxBodyBytes:
    Type: Number
    Default: 8192
  QueryLimit:
    Type: Number
    Default: 50
  EmailHashSalt:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    NoEcho: true
    Description: >
      Server secret salting the stored one-way email hash (used for moderation only; the hash is never
      returned). Set to a long random string; rotating it disconnects old hashes from new ones.

Conditions:
  # Which environment this is, is derived from the STACK NAME — not an external parameter. Production
  # is the one canonical stack named `tldr-app`; its table name is then pinned (below) to the exact
  # legacy `tldr-comments`. Nothing passed at deploy time can make prod point at a different table.
  # Any other stack name (tldr-app-dev, or an ad-hoc tldr-app-<x>) is non-prod and gets its own
  # stack-scoped table, so dev/sandbox testing can never read or write prod data.
  IsProd: !Equals [!Ref AWS::StackName, tldr-app]

Globals:
  Function:
    Runtime: nodejs22.x
    Architectures:
      - x86_64
    Timeout: 10
    MemorySize: 256
    Environment:
      Variables:
        NODE_OPTIONS: --enable-source-maps
        TABLE_NAME: !Ref CommentsTable
        MAX_BODY_BYTES: !Ref MaxBodyBytes
        QUERY_LIMIT: !Ref QueryLimit
        RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE: !Ref RateLimitPerMinute
        EMAIL_HASH_SALT: !Ref EmailHashSalt

Resources:
  CommentsTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    # The one irreplaceable-state resource. Retain on delete AND on replace; PITR for restore-to-second.
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      # prod (stack tldr-app) => the exact legacy name, HARD-CODED in source so it can't be overridden
      # from outside (renaming would REPLACE the table — see UpdateReplacePolicy and the frozen-KeySchema
      # note below). Any other stack => a stack-scoped table (e.g. tldr-app-dev => tldr-app-dev-comments),
      # so it's physically distinct from prod's data store.
      TableName: !If [IsProd, tldr-comments, !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-comments']
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      # FROZEN: editing the base table's KeySchema / AttributeDefinitions for pageId/commentId REPLACES
      # the table — a new EMPTY table; the data does NOT follow. Treat any changeset showing
      # "Replacement: True" here as a hard stop. Adding a GSI (below) is a separate, additive
      # UpdateTable operation — it does NOT touch the base KeySchema and does not replace the table.
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: pageId
          AttributeType: S
        - AttributeName: commentId
          AttributeType: S
        - AttributeName: categoryPageId
          AttributeType: S
        - AttributeName: voteCount
          AttributeType: N
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: pageId
          KeyType: HASH
        - AttributeName: commentId
          KeyType: RANGE
      # Issue #26 (link-hover preview): "the leading comment for pageId+category" needs a query the
      # base table can't answer (its only key is pageId+commentId, sorted by creation time, not votes).
      # `categoryPageId` (= "<pageId>#<category>") is written ONLY on comment items (handler.mjs), so
      # this GSI is naturally SPARSE — vote items and rate-limit counters never carry it and so never
      # appear here. `voteCount` already updates atomically via the existing vote TransactWriteItems
      # (handleVote), so the GSI tracks it with no new write path. A Query keyed on categoryPageId with
      # ScanIndexForward=false, Limit=1 returns the top-voted comment; ties (equal top voteCount) break
      # arbitrarily (DynamoDB's tie order, not a documented contract) — acceptable for a "leading
      # comment" preview. KNOWN LIMITATION: a GSI only indexes items that already carry its key
      # attributes, so comments written BEFORE this shipped are invisible to this index until rewritten
      # — there is no backfill (dev/docs/architecture.md §5.3).
      GlobalSecondaryIndexes:
        - IndexName: CategoryRankIndex
          KeySchema:
            - AttributeName: categoryPageId
              KeyType: HASH
            - AttributeName: voteCount
              KeyType: RANGE
          Projection:
            ProjectionType: ALL
      PointInTimeRecoverySpecification:
        PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled: true
      # Per-author rate-limit counter items carry an `expiresAt` (epoch seconds) and self-delete.
      # Real comment items have no such attribute, so TTL never touches them.
      TimeToLiveSpecification:
        AttributeName: expiresAt
        Enabled: true
      SSESpecification:
        SSEEnabled: true

  CommentsApi:
    Type: AWS::Serverless::HttpApi
    Properties:
      # API Gateway answers the CORS preflight (OPTIONS) itself, unauthenticated, before routing.
      CorsConfiguration:
        AllowOrigins:
          - !Ref AllowedExtensionOrigin
        AllowMethods:
          - GET
          - POST
          # DELETE is the vote toggle-off (RemoveVote, issue #22). Without it here the browser's
          # preflight for a DELETE gets no Access-Control-Allow-Origin and un-voting fails with a CORS
          # error ("No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header… / Failed to fetch") — visible only in a
          # real browser, never in a unit test.
          - DELETE
          - OPTIONS
        AllowHeaders:
          - authorization
          - content-type
          # The client attaches X-Client-Version (version telemetry, issue #29) to every request. A
          # custom header makes even the public GET a non-simple request, so the browser preflights
          # it — this MUST list the header or the preflight fails and reads/posts break in-browser.
          - x-client-version
        MaxAge: 600
      Auth:
        Authorizers:
          GoogleJwt:
            IdentitySource: $request.header.Authorization
            JwtConfiguration:
              issuer: https://accounts.google.com
              audience:
                - !Ref GoogleClientId
        # No DefaultAuthorizer: routes opt in. GET /comments stays PUBLIC — reads are public by
        # design (a community-notes product; every viewer sees the same list). Writes are gated.

  CommentsFunction:
    Type: AWS::Serverless::Function
    Properties:
      CodeUri: ./
      # The esbuild builder writes a single entry point to <artifact>/handler.js (the src/ prefix is
      # stripped — esbuild's default outbase is the entry's own dir), so the Handler is handler.handler.
      Handler: handler.handler
      Events:
        PostComment:
          Type: HttpApi
          Properties:
            ApiId: !Ref CommentsApi
            Method: POST
            Path: /comments
            Auth:
              Authorizer: GoogleJwt
        GetComments:
          Type: HttpApi
          Properties:
            ApiId: !Ref CommentsApi
            Method: GET
            Path: /comments
            # No Auth => public read.
        GetTopComment:
          Type: HttpApi
          Properties:
            ApiId: !Ref CommentsApi
            Method: GET
            Path: /comments/top
            # No Auth => public read, same as GetComments (issue #26, the CategoryRankIndex GSI above).
        CastVote:
          Type: HttpApi
          Properties:
            ApiId: !Ref CommentsApi
            Method: POST
            Path: /comments/{commentId}/vote
            Auth:
              Authorizer: GoogleJwt
        RemoveVote:
          Type: HttpApi
          Properties:
            ApiId: !Ref CommentsApi
            Method: DELETE
            Path: /comments/{commentId}/vote
            Auth:
              Authorizer: GoogleJwt
      Policies:
        - Statement:
            - Effect: Allow
              # Voting writes two items in one TransactWriteItems (the vote item + the comment's
              # voteCount); a toggle-off deletes the vote item. DynamoDB authorizes a transaction by
              # its UNDERLYING per-item actions (there is no dynamodb:TransactWriteItems action), so
              # PutItem/UpdateItem/DeleteItem together cover both votes and posts. (issue #22)
              Action:
                - dynamodb:PutItem
                - dynamodb:Query
                - dynamodb:UpdateItem
                - dynamodb:DeleteItem
              # A GSI Query is authorized against the INDEX's own ARN, not just the table's (issue #26,
              # GetTopComment querying CategoryRankIndex) — the table ARN alone is insufficient for that.
              Resource:
                - !GetAtt CommentsTable.Arn
                - !Sub '${CommentsTable.Arn}/index/CategoryRankIndex'
    Metadata:
      BuildMethod: esbuild
      BuildProperties:
        EntryPoints:
          - src/handler.mjs
        Target: node22
        Format: cjs
        Minify: true
        Sourcemap: true
        # Bundle the AWS SDK: the managed runtime does NOT ship @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb, and its
        # @aws-sdk minor drifts across runtime patches. Bundling makes the artifact deterministic.
        External: []

  # Pre-create the log group so we own its retention (Lambda's auto-created group never expires).
  CommentsFunctionLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub /aws/lambda/${CommentsFunction}
      RetentionInDays: 30

Outputs:
  ApiUrl:
    Description: Base URL for the API. Clients POST/GET <ApiUrl>/comments.
    Value: !Sub https://${CommentsApi}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com
  CommentsTableName:
    Value: !Ref CommentsTable

[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/TLDR/sha/578ab8ab92f8f0659b0b6bf56ae113802745eb5d/contents/.github/workflows/deploy.yml] name: deploy

# Deploys the server app stack to AWS via GitHub OIDC (no stored keys). The job is GATED on the
# repository VARIABLE AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN: until the owner sets it (and GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID), the job is
# SKIPPED (gray) — never a red failure. (A variable, not a secret, because secrets aren't readable in
# a job-level `if:`, so a secret gate can't skip cleanly. The role ARN is not sensitive.)
#
# Promotion model: a push to main with server changes auto-deploys DEV (the always-current sandbox),
# so every merged server change is immediately exercisable end-to-end. PROD is NEVER automatic — it's
# a deliberate manual promotion (workflow_dispatch, environment: prod) you run once a change has been
# verified in dev.
#
# Account model: DEV and PROD live in SEPARATE AWS ACCOUNTS (dev/docs/dev-account-runbook.md). Each account
# has its own GitHub-OIDC deploy role trusting this repo+branch, so the job assumes a role PER ENVIRONMENT:
# prod => AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN (prod account), dev => AWS_DEV_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN (dev account). Until the dev role
# variable is set, dev FALLS BACK to AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN, so this is a no-op before the dev account exists.
# Both roles trust refs/heads/main, so neither trust policy changes.

on:
  # Push to main that changes something the app stack actually DEPLOYS => auto-deploy DEV only (prod is
  # manual, via workflow_dispatch below). This is an allowlist on purpose: only the deploy inputs — the
  # template, the Lambda source + its deps, the deploy config, and the shared canonical sources — should
  # trigger a deploy. Tests, dev scripts, and the README are intentionally excluded, so a docs/test-only
  # commit doesn't spin up a whole deploy job just to produce an empty changeset.
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'server/template.yaml'
      - 'server/samconfig.toml'
      - 'server/src/**'
      - 'server/package.json'
      - 'server/package-lock.json'
      - 'shared/**'
      - '.github/workflows/deploy.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: 'Environment to deploy. prod = deliberate promotion (tldr-app); dev = sandbox (tldr-app-dev).'
        type: choice
        options: [prod, dev]
        default: prod

permissions:
  id-token: write # assume the AWS role via OIDC
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: deploy-server
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: ${{ vars.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN != '' && vars.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID != '' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      # Resolve the target environment once. A push to main auto-deploys DEV; a manual dispatch honors
      # its input (prod = the deliberate promotion). Each env maps to a codified samconfig section
      # (prod => default, dev => dev), which carries the stack name — the template derives prod-vs-dev
      # from that stack name, so there's no Environment parameter to pass. The env also selects WHICH
      # ACCOUNT'S OIDC role to assume (prod vs dev account); dev falls back to the prod role until the
      # dev-account role variable exists. Both roles trust refs/heads/main, so neither stays un-scoped.
      - name: Resolve target environment
        id: env
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
            ENV="${{ inputs.environment }}"
          else
            ENV="dev"
          fi
          if [ "$ENV" = "prod" ]; then
            CONFIG="default"; STACK="tldr-app"; ROLE="${{ vars.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}"
          else
            CONFIG="$ENV"; STACK="tldr-app-$ENV"; ROLE="${{ vars.AWS_DEV_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}"
          fi
          # Pre-migration fallback: no dedicated dev-account role yet => use the prod-account role.
          if [ -z "$ROLE" ]; then ROLE="${{ vars.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}"; fi
          if [ -z "$ROLE" ]; then
            echo "::error::No deploy role configured for env '$ENV' (set AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN / AWS_DEV_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN)."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "name=$ENV" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "config=$CONFIG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "stack=$STACK" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "role=$ROLE" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Deploying environment '$ENV' (samconfig env '$CONFIG') to stack '$STACK'." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: server/package-lock.json

      - name: Install server deps
        working-directory: server
        run: npm ci

      - uses: aws-actions/setup-sam@v3
        with:
          use-installer: true

      # SAM's esbuild builder needs esbuild on PATH (its scratch install is production-only).
      - name: Install esbuild on PATH (for SAM's esbuild builder)
        run: npm install -g esbuild@0.24.0

      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ steps.env.outputs.role }}
          aws-region: il-central-1

      - name: sam build
        working-directory: server
        run: sam build

      - name: sam deploy (app stack)
        working-directory: server
        run: |
          sam deploy --config-env ${{ steps.env.outputs.config }} \
            --no-confirm-changeset \
            --no-fail-on-empty-changeset \
            --parameter-overrides "GoogleClientId=${{ vars.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }} AllowedExtensionOrigin=${{ vars.ALLOWED_EXTENSION_ORIGIN || '*' }} EmailHashSalt=${{ secrets.EMAIL_HASH_SALT }}"

      # Stack termination protection can't be expressed in the template body; set it via the API after
      # deploy. Idempotent — re-enabling an already-protected stack is a no-op — so it runs every deploy.
      # prod only: the dev stack must stay deletable (`sam delete --config-env dev`) for teardown.
      - name: Enable termination protection on the app stack
        if: ${{ steps.env.outputs.name == 'prod' }}
        run: |
          aws cloudformation update-termination-protection \
            --enable-termination-protection \
            --stack-name ${{ steps.env.outputs.stack }} \
            --region il-central-1

# (per-project-scheduling DESIGN §3). A thin shim: all logic lives in the
# vendored engine, so this file changes rarely (schema and behavior changes ride
# the vendor refresh, not edits here). It runs hourly on a repo-hashed minute
# constrained to :10–:50 — spreading the fleet, dodging GitHub's :00 stampede,
# and staying clear of the hour boundary the slot math anchors on.
#
# The minute below is a placeholder; bootstrap/vendoring rewrites it to this
# repo's stable hashed minute in :10–:50, computed by
# `node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs <owner/repo>`
# (scheduler-workflow-shape enforces the range; baselining re-derives the value to
# catch drift). `workflow_dispatch` allows a manual run; the concurrency group
# serializes runs so a slow run and its successor never overlap.
#
# A manual run may carry `overrides` — ONE free-form `KEY=value` string, because
# GitHub cannot declare arbitrary named inputs. It reaches the engine as
# `CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES`, and the engine understands exactly one key:
# `FORCE_TASKS=<comma-separated task ids>`.
# It runs those tasks even though their slot has already passed, and
# WITHOUT consulting their preconditions — forcing is the operator's decision, so
# nothing asks the task whether it agrees. The engine learns "run these ids",
# never what any of them do, and no task declaration mentions forcing at all.
name: Claudinite scheduler

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '20 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      overrides:
        description: 'Manual-run overrides: comma-separated KEY=value. FORCE_TASKS=<task ids> runs those tasks unconditionally, even when their slot has passed, e.g. FORCE_TASKS=baselining.'
        required: false
        default: ''

concurrency:
  group: claudinite-scheduler
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write        # read the repo + vendored engine; baselining's deliver() pushes the maintenance branch (agent-preprocessing §7/E4)
  issues: write          # file / label / close dispatch issues
  pull-requests: write   # baselining's deliver() opens the per-cycle maintenance PR and arms auto-merge
  actions: write         # read the run ledger (last successful run) for due-slot math, AND
                         # dispatch a workflow a task drives (store-release fires the release
                         # orchestrator's daily leg) — creating a workflow_dispatch event needs
                         # write, not read, and `read` silently 403s the POST

jobs:
  schedule:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Evaluate schedule and dispatch due tasks
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # Empty on every scheduled run — `inputs` is only populated by
          # workflow_dispatch. The engine reads only FORCE_TASKS out of it.
          CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES: ${{ inputs.overrides }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/run.mjs

  # A scheduled run reaches no one when it goes red, so escalate a whole-run
  # failure to a human-visible `workflow-failure` issue (DESIGN §3.6,
  # gha/scheduled-failure-escalation). Converges to ONE open issue by a fixed
  # title (create-or-comment), and ensures the label first since a first-run
  # failure may precede the scheduler's own label-ensure.
  report-failure:
    needs: schedule
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const { owner, repo } = context.repo;
            const title = 'Claudinite scheduler run failed';
            await github.rest.issues.createLabel({ owner, repo, name: 'workflow-failure', color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite scheduler: a scheduler run or task failed' }).catch(() => {});
            const run = `${context.serverUrl}/${owner}/${repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`;
            const body = `The Claudinite scheduler run failed: ${run}`;
            const found = await github.rest.search.issuesAndPullRequests({ q: `repo:${owner}/${repo} is:issue is:open in:title "${title}"` });
            if (found.data.total_count > 0) await github.rest.issues.createComment({ owner, repo, issue_number: found.data.items[0].number, body });
            else await github.rest.issues.create({ owner, repo, title, labels: ['workflow-failure'], body });

![spec-driven-product](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-YjX4Ow/packs/spec-driven-product/badge.svg "spec-driven-product") ![executable-requirements](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-YjX4Ow/packs/executable-requirements/badge.svg "executable-requirements") ![flutter](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-YjX4Ow/packs/flutter/badge.svg "flutter") ![android](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-YjX4Ow/packs/android/badge.svg "android") ![ios](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-YjX4Ow/packs/ios/badge.svg "ios") ![firebase](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-YjX4Ow/packs/firebase/badge.svg "firebase") ![node](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-YjX4Ow/packs/node/badge.svg "node") ![basics](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-YjX4Ow/packs/basics/badge.svg "basics") ![barriers](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-YjX4Ow/packs/barriers/badge.svg "barriers") ![git-github](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-YjX4Ow/packs/git-github/badge.svg "git-github") ![tidy-repo](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-YjX4Ow/packs/tidy-repo/badge.svg "tidy-repo") ![grow_with_claudinite](../../../../../tmp/claudinite-canon-YjX4Ow/packs/grow_with_claudinite/badge.svg "grow_with_claudinite")<!-- /claudinite:packs -->

A hyperlocal messaging app. When you send a message, it is delivered to exactly
the people who were physically near you at the moment you sent it — a
**whisper** reaches 150 m, a **shout** reaches 1,500 m — and never to anyone
who arrives later. Every recipient keeps a durable personal feed of everything
they received, even while the app was in their pocket.

The full design (data model, fan-out architecture, security rules, threat
model) is in [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md). The UI's
dependency-injection architecture is
[docs/UI-ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/UI-ARCHITECTURE.md); the dev/prod
environment plan is [docs/ENVIRONMENTS.md](docs/ENVIRONMENTS.md).

## Repository layout

```
app/                    Flutter client (ports/adapters — see docs/UI-ARCHITECTURE.md)
firebase/               Firebase project root (everything the Firebase CLI reads)
  firebase.json         Firebase project config
  .firebaserc           project aliases (committed default = dev, always)
  firestore.rules       Firestore security rules
  firestore.indexes.json  Firestore indexes (empty — single-field indexes suffice)
  functions/            Cloud Functions (TypeScript, Node 22)
dev/requirements/       executable UI requirements: spec, cases, goldens, runners
docs/                   design, UI architecture, environments
```

## Prerequisites

- Flutter SDK (stable channel)
- Node 22
- [Firebase CLI](https://firebase.google.com/docs/cli) (`npm install -g firebase-tools`)
- A Firebase project on the **Blaze** plan (required for Cloud Functions)
- [FlutterFire CLI](https://firebase.flutter.dev/docs/cli/) (`dart pub global activate flutterfire_cli`)

## Firebase setup

Everything below targets the **dev** project — the committed default in
`.firebaserc`. Production doesn't exist yet and nothing in this repo will
ever point at it by accident; the plan for the split (and why only
store-installed apps will talk to prod) is
[docs/ENVIRONMENTS.md](docs/ENVIRONMENTS.md).

1. **Create the dev Firebase project** at
   <https://console.firebase.google.com> (suggested id:
   `shouts-whispers-dev` — update `firebase/.firebaserc` if you pick another) and
   upgrade it to the Blaze plan.

2. **Enable Google sign-in**: in the console, Authentication → Sign-in
   method → add **Google** as a provider.

3. **Configure the Flutter app**:

   ```sh
   cd app
   flutterfire configure
   ```

   This generates `lib/firebase_options.dart` (replacing the committed
   placeholder, which throws with setup instructions until you do this) and
   the platform config files (`google-services.json` /
   `GoogleService-Info.plist`).

4. **Android only — register your SHA-1 fingerprint** (required for Google
   Sign-In). Get the debug-keystore fingerprint with:

   ```sh
   keytool -list -v -keystore ~/.android/debug.keystore \
     -alias androiddebugkey -storepass android -keypass android
   ```

   Add the SHA-1 under Project settings → Your apps → Android app in the
   Firebase console, then re-download `google-services.json` (or re-run
   `flutterfire configure`).

5. **Deploy the backend** (functions and Firestore rules), from the
   `firebase/` project root:

   ```sh
   cd firebase
   npm --prefix functions install
   firebase deploy --only functions,firestore
   ```

   The deploy's predeploy hook compiles the TypeScript automatically. (The
   Firebase CLI locates the project by the `firebase.json` in `firebase/`;
   from elsewhere in the repo, pass `--config firebase/firebase.json`.)

## Run the app

```sh
cd app
flutter pub get
flutter run
```

The app asks for location permission on first launch — it needs a GPS fix
before you can send, and it reports presence heartbeats while foregrounded.
The map uses OpenStreetMap tiles, so no maps API key is needed.

## Development

Cloud Functions (`firebase/functions/`):

```sh
cd firebase/functions
npm run build   # tsc
npm test        # vitest — pure-function tests, no emulator needed
```

Flutter app (`app/`):

```sh
flutter analyze
flutter test
```

Executable UI requirements (`dev/requirements/` — the UI spec run as tests;
see its [README](dev/requirements/README.md)):

```sh
cd dev/requirements
flutter pub get                # first time
flutter test                   # coverage gate + screens + sagas + behaviors + logic
python3 refresh_goldens.py     # regenerate goldens + gallery (review step!)
```

Every screen state, gesture, and multi-step user saga renders and asserts
against scripted fakes — no device, no Firebase project, no network. The
spec ([dev/requirements/requirements.md](dev/requirements/requirements.md))
embeds the rendered screenshots inline, so reading it is reviewing the app.

## Current limitations (v1)

Deliberate cuts, documented in [docs/DESIGN.md §7](docs/DESIGN.md):

- **Foreground-only presence.** If the app is backgrounded for more than
  5 minutes, your presence goes stale and you stop receiving messages —
  as far as the system is concerned, you're not there.
- **No anti-spoofing.** A client can lie about its GPS coordinates to send
  into, or receive from, an area it isn't in.
- **No moderation.** There is a 5-second server-side send cooldown, but no
  content moderation, blocking, or reporting.

[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/gRatio/sha/163a2b8c91e524dc5dd793b69dc93ec320917246/contents/docs/reference/external_datasets.md] # External datasets — public EM cross-sections for the corpus

Curated sources of myelinated-axon EM cross-sections like `data/samples/`
(TEM, dark concentric myelin on a light field), for growing the corpus and for
validation. Ranked by fit = modality match × g-ratio availability × ease.

**Two ground-truth tiers — they plug into different harnesses:**

- **g-ratio labels** (a published g per image, no masks) → validate the
  *number* via `validate_external.py`. Cannot score segmentation IoU.
- **segmentation masks** (per-pixel axon/myelin) → score *segmentation* via the
  `evaluate_segmentation.py` / `report.py` path, and derive per-axon g with
  `gratio/reference.py`. This is the tier the three `data/samples/` sit in.

Do not mix them: fabricating masks for a g-labelled set to force it into the IoU
harness violates the "GT is annotated, never invented" rule (see user_masks.md).

## Tier 1 — TEM cross-sections WITH published g-ratios

### macaque_cc  ✅ ingested → `data/external/macaque_cc/`
8 TEM images of one cynomolgus macaque corpus callosum, 9.144 nm/px, ~21×28 µm,
dense myelinated axons. **Aggregate g-ratio per image** (Table 1: g_agg
0.67–0.75). **CC-BY 4.0.** Visual dead-ringer for `sample_03`. Fetched from
Europe PMC by `data/external/macaque_cc/fetch.py`.
- Paper: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4510539/ (DOI 10.1016/j.dib.2015.05.019)
- Ground truth: **g-ratio labels** (image-level), no masks.

## Tier 2 — TEM/SEM cross-sections WITH masks (→ per-axon g via reference.py)

| Dataset | What | Access | License |
|---|---|---|---|
| **White Matter Microscopy DB** | The bulk source. Curated CNS+PNS white-matter EM across 7 institutions, multi-species, **SEM+TEM**, many with axon/myelin masks. What AxonDeepSeg is built on. | [osf.io/yp4qg](https://osf.io/yp4qg/) (OSF API for scripted pulls) | Free, per-dataset attribution |
| **AxonDeepSeg SEM** | 10 rat spinal-cord SEM crops + manual masks. `git clone`-able. ⚠️ SEM = *bright* myelin (inverted vs our TEM) — needs a polarity flip. | [github.com/axondeepseg/data_axondeepseg_sem](https://github.com/axondeepseg/data_axondeepseg_sem) | MIT |
| **AxonDeepSeg TEM** | Mouse-brain TEM patches, 0.01 µm/px + macaque, axon/myelin masks. Our samples' own modality. | in WMMDB / neuropoly | — |
| **AxonCallosumEM** | Whole mouse corpus callosum (Rett model), dense axon **and** myelin-sheath masks, very large. | [arXiv:2307.02464](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.02464) | see paper |

## Tier 3 — bulk / 3D / specialized (no per-image g table)

- **gACSON** — 6 SBEM 3D volumes, rat cortex (sham + TBI); myelin-thickness & g
  morphometry. Take 2D slices. MIT: [github.com/AndreaBehan/g-ACSON](https://github.com/AndreaBehan/g-ACSON)
- **Human superficial white matter, 3D multibeam SEM** (NeuroImage 2025) —
  128,285 segmented myelinated axons. Big/3D.
- **nanotomy.org** — human MS-vs-control brain, large-scale 2D STEM, open access,
  browsable viewer (blocks scripted download).

## The scale gotcha (why external data isn't drop-in)

Our samples are *zoomed* (1–5 axons). WMMDB/macaque fields are *wide* (dozens–
hundreds of small axons). The pipeline is tuned for the zoomed view
(`min_axon_frac=0.02`), so on a full macaque field it detects **0 axons**, and
on a crop it finds only the biggest 2–3 and over-extends the myelin band. A
scale-aware / multi-scale pass is needed before these segment cleanly; until
then `validate_external.py` is the harness that gap is measured against.
